  • Reference

    Summarise threshold-based metrics for model and cross-validation predictions

    cv_summary_table.Rd
    cv_summary_table(
  cv_method_1,
  cv_method_2,
  model,
  reported_status,
  threshold,
  names = c(cv_method_1 = "cv_method_1", cv_method_2 = "cv_method_2", model = "model")
)

    Arguments

    cv_method_1

    Numeric vector. Predictions from the first cross-validation method.

    cv_method_2

    Numeric vector. Predictions from the second cross-validation method. Must be the same length and of the same scale as cv_method_1.

    model

    Numeric vector of model predictions used for threshold-based classification. Must be the same length and of the same scale as cv_method_1.

    reported_status

    Numeric, factor, or logical vector indicating observed status for each observation. Values equal to 1 are treated as "reported positive", values equal to 0 as "reported negative". Must be the same length as cv_method_1.

    threshold

    Numeric. Threshold used to classify predictions as positive or negative. Must be on the same scale as cv_method_1.

    names

    Named character vector of length 3 giving row names for the output. Must have names cv_method_1, cv_method_2, and model. Values are used as row labels in the output.

    Value

    A data.frame with three rows (one per method) and columns: true_positive_rate, percent_over_threshold, and count_over_threshold.

    Details

    For each method, the following are returned:

    • true_positive_rate: percentage of reported positive cases (where reported_status == 1) with predictions above the threshold

    • count_over_threshold: number of predictions above the threshold

    • percent_over_threshold: percentage of all predictions above the threshold

    See also

    compute_summary_metrics

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cv_summary_table(
  cv_method_1 = loo_lodds,
  cv_method_2 = kfold_lodds,
  model_predictions = predictions$prediction_lodds,
  reported_status = predictions$host_status,
  threshold = thr_intercepts["threshold"]
)
} # }
